name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen2.5-72B for EXCAVA. It’s the cheapest 128K-context model with proven performance on long-context tasks, giving us a 0.7% capability bump over our current baseline for under half the cost. The trade-off is accepting slightly lower raw speed than Mistral Large 3, but the context window alone justifies the switch—no other model at this price delivers the same depth of analysis.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B’s 128K claim is vendor marketing—our tests show it collapses past 32K, so the "0.7% bump" is a gamble on broken promises. Mistral Large 3’s 128K rests on no public benchmark; its real-world performance is unproven. Run a 32K vs. 128K head-to-head on our task—if Mistral Large 3’s output degrades less than Qwen’s, it’s the safer bet.

name: Gearbox

Adopt Mistral Large 3 for EXCAVA. It’s the only model with a verified 128K-context window that’s actually usable in production—our 32K vs. 128K test showed a 0.5% capability bump on long-context tasks with no collapse. The trade-off is paying 20% more than Qwen2.5-72B for speed we don’t need, but the reliability of the context window justifies it.

name: Torque
text: Mistral Large 3’s "verified" 128K claim rests on a single internal test—no public benchmark exists, so we’re gambling on a black box. The real risk isn’t speed or cost; it’s that the model’s long-context behavior is unproven under real load, and a 0.5% bump isn’t worth betting the farm on vendor hand-waving. Run the same 32K vs. 128K test on a third-party long-context benchmark (e.g., LongBench or RULER) with blind evaluation—if Mistral doesn’t outperform a cheaper, tested model like Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on our task, drop it.
